pipeline.evidence: R1 signal re-interpretation + fresh support validation. (1) A noiseless blur_motion:1 simulation reproduces EVERY step-level signal of the target: block_boundary 0.990 vs 0.987 (clean 0.983), unique_G 238 vs 238 (clean 254), dct_zero_ratio 0.568 vs 0.521 (clean 0.279), wavelet sigma 0.74 vs 0.74, spatial_corr 0.813 vs 0.819, cross_ch 0.947 vs 0.949, residual_intensity_corr -0.272 vs -0.281, gm_ratio 0.573 vs 0.582, spectral_slope -1.354 vs -1.363, ratio 1.034 vs 1.041, variance_ratio 0.992 vs 0.992, mean_shift -0.3 vs -0.4. (2) R1 pair3 test hit 65.91 dB / CI 10/10 with blur_motion:1 when the random angle happened to align -> near pixel-exact reproduction, proving subtype+severity and excluding any extra step (JPEG/noise/global). Other pairs' lower PSNR (25-37 dB) is pure random-angle mismatch (same function, same pair3 gave 22.69 dB in R0). (3) 'BLUR_UNLIKELY' and 'FFT_anisotropy=0.00/PCA=0.0' in the R0 report were artifacts: run_full_analysis sets has_noise from the step2 verdict string (low-confidence GAUSSIAN_YCrCb, sigma=0.74), which forces the slope_ratio branch (1.041<1.08) instead of gm_ratio<0.62; step3 returns early before computing residual_anisotropy/PCA, so those 0.00 values were never measured. Verdict stays UNCERTAIN per SKILL C4 because motion samples a random angle per call, so PSNR cannot always exceed 40 dB even when correct.
